Adalar: The Princes' Islands in the Sea of Marmara. Car-free streets, wooden mansions and pine woods, reached by ferry. Mostly summer and second homes.
Arnavutköy: A large, fast-growing district on the northern edge of the European side, home to Istanbul Airport. Newer residential projects and plenty of open land.
Ataşehir: A modern Asian-side district of residential towers and offices, next to the Istanbul Finance Center. Popular with families and professionals.
Avcılar: A western European-side district on the Sea of Marmara and Küçükçekmece Lake, with a large university campus and good-value housing.
Bahçelievler: A dense, central residential district on the European side, close to the airport road, metro and metrobus lines.
Bakırköy: A long-established seaside district on the European side, with a coastal promenade, shopping streets and good transport links.
Bayrampaşa: A compact, central residential district on the European side, well connected by metro and close to the old city.
Bağcılar: One of the most populous districts on the European side, with busy shopping areas and new projects along the metro lines.
Başakşehir: A planned district on the European side with large residential compounds, parks and the city hospital. A favourite with families.
Beykoz: The greenest district on the Asian Bosphorus, with forests, villages and waterfront mansions stretching up towards the Black Sea.
Beylikdüzü: A western European-side district of newer apartment complexes and wide avenues, popular with international buyers for its value.
Beyoğlu: Istanbul's cultural heart around Taksim, İstiklal Street and Galata, with historic buildings, nightlife and Golden Horn views.
Beşiktaş: A lively district on the European Bosphorus, from Ortaköy and Bebek to Levent's business towers. Among the most sought-after addresses.
Büyükçekmece: A coastal district on the far west of the European side, around a lagoon and lake, with low-rise homes and new seaside projects.
Çatalca: A rural district at the western edge of the city, with farmland, forests and villages. Mostly detached homes and land.
Çekmeköy: A green Asian-side district near the Ömerli forest, with villas, gated compounds and a metro connection.
Esenler: A central European-side district best known for the main intercity bus terminal, with dense housing and metro access.
Esenyurt: A very large district on the western European side with many newer apartment projects at accessible prices.
Eyüpsultan: A district stretching from the historic Eyüp Sultan Mosque on the Golden Horn up to Göktürk's villas and the northern forests.
Fatih: The historic peninsula: Hagia Sophia, the Grand Bazaar and the old city walls. Mostly older buildings and some restoration projects.
Gaziosmanpaşa: A central residential district on the European side, undergoing a lot of urban renewal with new apartment blocks.
Güngören: A small, dense residential district on the European side, close to the airport road and the shopping streets of Merter.
Kadıköy: The Asian side's liveliest district, from Moda's seafront and cafés to Fenerbahçe and the long Caddebostan coast.
Kartal: An Asian-side district on the Sea of Marmara, with a long coastline, the metro line and many urban renewal projects.
Kağıthane: A central European-side district next to Levent and Şişli, transformed by new residential towers and offices.
Küçükçekmece: A large western European-side district around Küçükçekmece Lake, mixing established neighbourhoods and new developments.
Maltepe: An Asian-side district with a long Marmara seafront park, metro access and many new residential projects.
Pendik: An Asian-side district near Sabiha Gökçen Airport and the high-speed train station, with marinas and seaside living.
Sancaktepe: A growing Asian-side district with newer residential compounds and metro access, close to the TEM motorway.
Sarıyer: The northern European Bosphorus, from Maslak's towers to İstinye, Tarabya and forest villages. Waterfront living and green space.
Silivri: A coastal district far to the west on the Sea of Marmara, with summer homes, beaches and quieter town life.
Sultanbeyli: An Asian-side residential district near Sabiha Gökçen Airport and the TEM motorway, with ongoing development.
Sultangazi: A northern European-side residential district with dense housing and new projects along the transport corridors.
Tuzla: The easternmost district on the Asian side, with shipyards, marinas, universities and seaside neighbourhoods.
Zeytinburnu: A European-side district on the Sea of Marmara next to the old city walls, with a seafront park and many new towers.
Ümraniye: A large Asian-side district with shopping centres, offices and new residential projects, close to the Finance Center.
Üsküdar: The historic Asian Bosphorus district facing the old city, with Maiden's Tower, mosques, Kuzguncuk's lanes and Çamlıca Hill.
Şile: A coastal district on the Black Sea at the far east of the city, known for beaches, forests and holiday homes.
Şişli: A central European-side district of business towers, shopping streets and residences, from Nişantaşı to Mecidiyeköy.
